tools.name: suppa_search_records
tools.description:
Search records of any entity. filters_json: [{field, value, comparator}]. fields_json: {field: true}.
Comparators: =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, like, not like, in, not in, between, not between,
is null, is not null. 'like' is a case-insensitive CONTAINS — send the bare text; the
platform adds % and escapes yours, so 'LMS.%' matches nothing. 'in' takes a JSON array,
'between' [from, to] or a period like "$this_month". Field paths may be dotted —
"stage.status.value", "owner.id" — and the value "$current-user" resolves to the
signed-in user's id.
match_any=true combines filters with OR instead of AND.
NESTED GROUPS: a filters_json entry may be {"operator": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]}
(nested to any depth), so (status=open AND owner=me) OR priority=high is ONE call.
An EMPTY result (or a 400) is auto-diagnosed with select/validate: if the query
references a field that does not exist you get "validation" naming it, not silence.
Returns {records, returned, has_more, next_offset, deleted_scope} — page with offset until has_more is false.

Enum fields read back as objects {value, title, id} — project them as
{"myEnum": {"value": true}} and read .value, not as a bare string.

SOFT-DELETED ROWS: deleted_scope='deleted' returns ONLY records that
suppa_delete_record removed — that is how you find the id to hand to
suppa_restore_record. 'all' returns live and removed together (removed
ones carry a non-null deletedAt; project it to tell them apart).

entity_name.description: Exact entity name, e.g. 'Tasks', 'Users' — see suppa_list_entities.

filters_json.description: JSON array of filters: [{"field": "status.value", "value": "active", "comparator": "="}]. 'like' = contains, bare text, no %; dotted paths allowed. An entry may also be a NESTED GROUP {"operator": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]} (shorthand {"or": [...]}), so (a AND b) OR c is one call.

fields_json.description: JSON projection of fields to return, e.g. {"id": true, "title": true, "owner": {"id": true, "fullName": true}}. Enums: {"myEnum": {"value": true}}.

search.description: Free-text search across the entity's searchable fields.

match_any.description: true = combine filters with OR instead of AND.

tools.name: suppa_query
tools.description:
Run ONE read-only SuppaSQL statement — POST /core/data/query, the endpoint the
builder's SQL charts and tables use. Check a chart/table SQL source with it before
writing the form: an incomplete one shows demo data, a wrong one fails at runtime.

SELECT / WITH only, one statement, no comments (SuppaSQL has none); anything else is
refused and nothing is sent. Runs with the caller's read permissions; deleted rows are
excluded. A missing LIMIT is added and a bigger literal one clamped, so at most `limit`
rows come back, with `truncated` and `columns` — the keys of every row, nested ones as
dot paths (owner.firstName): a TABLE column's key. `chart_note` says when the same
text fails as a CHART source: a chart needs LIMIT 10000 or less (it sends LIMIT 10001,
refused with query.row_limit). A CHART's sqlCategoryColumn / sqlValueColumns[].key is a
field's last segment (firstName) or the alias of a COMPUTED item (COUNT, CASE,
TO_CHAR…); never alias a plain field in a chart query — the chart reads it by its path
and shows nothing. Writing one: suppa_sql_kb (check a draft offline first); slow, or
failing for some role: suppa_query_analyze, once.

query.description: The SuppaSQL statement, e.g. SELECT "stage.name", COUNT("id") AS "n" FROM Tasks GROUP BY "stage.name" LIMIT 100 — as a chart: sqlCategoryColumn "name", sqlValueColumns [{"key": "n"}].

bind_params_json.description: JSON object of bind values for $name / $1 / = ANY($arr), e.g. {"owner": 479}. $current-user is set by the server, but not in an FB2 widget; $now / $current_date never are (use NOW()).

tools.name: suppa_sql_kb
tools.description:
The SuppaSQL skill (skills/writing-suppa-sql): write, check and tune a query for
suppa_query, a chart / table SQL source or an application. Offline; touches no tenant.

rules      the cycle, request discipline, the five rules   cheatsheet  goal → query
mistakes   common mistakes and their fix
check      a draft's TEXT: what the platform refuses ($now, CURRENT_DATE, LEFT JOIN,
           LIMIT > 10000…) and the measured slow shapes it shows (P1–P14)
ref        topic language|unsupported|performance|practices|analytics|actions|http-api,
           section = a heading (e.g. P14); a long topic without one lists its sections

mode.description: Which part of the skill to read, or 'check' a draft.

topic.description: mode='ref': the reference. Omit to list them with their sections.

section.description: mode='ref': words of a heading ('P14', 'Bind parameters'); '*' = the whole reference.

bind_params_json.description: mode='check': the bind values you will send, so a bound $name is not flagged.

tools.name: suppa_query_analyze
tools.description:
ONE analysis of a FINAL SuppaSQL query on the active tenant: the plan for you and for every
role (× the full-rights cost, the access rules' share, the roles it FAILS for), the size
and indexes of the tables it reads, and the actions to PROPOSE — create / rebuild / drop an
index, rewrite the query; none is applied. Plan only: nothing runs unless run_query=true.
Needs the owner group or DATABASE_ANALYTICS.VIEW. Up to 13 requests; /query-analyze allows
10 calls a minute per user — iterate on drafts with suppa_sql_kb mode='check', analyse the
final one once. On a rate limit it stops and reports what it has: do not repeat it.

query.description: The SuppaSQL statement, as the chart, table or application sends it.

tools.name: suppa_update_entity_options
tools.description:
Turn the platform's per-entity FEATURES on or off (POST
/core/builder/<entity>/update-options) — a narrower alternative to editing the
entity that touches only options. This is the only way to reach comments,
reactions, hierarchy, folders, change history, browsing history, global search,
time tracking, favorites, pinned, approvals, checklists, recurrence, reminders,
notification mutes and customFields (per-context extra columns — see
suppa_add_custom_field) from here; send only the ones you are changing.

NOT A FREE TOGGLE: enabling an option CREATES the side table that backs it, and
recurrence / reminders / notificationMutes / timeTracking / pinned also refresh
the cache of the corresponding system entity. It is a schema change.

RESTRICTIONS: on an entity the tenant does not own (initiator 'system' or
'application') only options.stateHistory and options.externalSource may change —
the platform answers 403 to the rest, so this server refuses the call first. A
system-GENERATED entity (a reserved suffix: Comments, Folders, CustomFields…)
refuses comments, customFields and six more — refused here too. The platform
answers with the APPLIED options, which
may be a subset of the request — anything missing is called out in the result.

tools.description:

  encrypt=false clears it.
- 'encrypted' is only allowed on a TEXT field, and it forces searchable, canFilter,
  canSort and canGroup off (plus unique, max_length, min_length, mask), so it
  cannot be combined with them in one call. Encrypting rewrites the existing rows.

one. A CUSTOM field is different: suppa_remove_custom_field parks it reversibly.
This tool edits a custom field too — pass entity_name='<Entity>CustomFields'.

Reads entities and their fields from Suppa 1.0 (configured via SUPPA_V1_API_KEY / SUPPA_V1_ACCESS_TOKEN

tools.name: suppa_validate_form_schema
tools.description:
Run the gate over a Suppa 2.0 form draft BEFORE writing it. Offline; touches no tenant.

The platform form builder's own STRUCTURAL checker: 37 error codes — unknown types and
props, bindings that resolve to nothing, malformed geometry and containment, bad option
values, collisions. It does NOT carry the authoring lints (an unbound select, an empty
container, a second Save): those live in the source agent's uxVerify pass, which is
not vendored here. Passing is structural, not editorial. It also refuses chart SQL the
runtime refuses or reads empty, warns on low contrast and heightless charts, and
compiles every widget's compiledRender as the builder does.

FOR AN EDIT PASS baseline_path, the form as it exists on the tenant: the component
manifest lags the live platform, so without it the tenant's own props read as errors.
Measured on every live form of a dev tenant: 59 of 96 cold, 73 as an edit.

passed=false means fix and re-run; passed=true WITH warnings is not a clean form.

tools.name: suppa_write_form_draft
tools.description:
Save a Suppa 2.0 form as a DRAFT on the tenant, through the builder's own save
(PUT /core/forms/:id/schema). It never publishes: what others see stays the published
version; a published form reads `editing`. The save appears in the builder's History.

The gate runs first, judged against the live form: what the form already has does not
block, a refusal or an error the draft adds and nothing is written. It compiles each
changed widget's compiledRender from its template; a hand-written one is never saved.
The row is read first and a read that does not clearly succeed ABORTS — merging over a
failed read is how a saved mobile layout and code-form vanish on a call returning 200.
Writes schema and settings; `variables` only when the draft lists some — the list is the
FULL state (an omitted variable is deleted), so an empty one is never sent and one that
drops the form's default variable is refused. mobileSchema, code, localizations, entity,
alias and parent are never sent; a child form's `schema.overrides` is preserved.

Refuses while someone else has the form open in the builder (lockedBy). Without
confirm=true it returns the plan and a `revision`; pass it back as expected_revision and
a form that moved since the preview is refused, not overwritten.

tools.name: suppa_validate_entity_code
tools.description:
Run the schema gate over an application repo's *.entity.ts / *.seed.ts / module files.

CALL THIS BEFORE REPORTING ANY ENTITY OR SEED FILE DONE. It is the same checker the
bundled suppa-entity-code skill names as its close-out gate, and it catches what tsc
cannot: an unregistered entity class (no table is ever created for it), a JS value in
'default' where a SQL string is required, a relation without a thunk, seed records that
duplicate on every restart — plus the house rules, which fail the gate:
  * a relation property must be typed to match its decorator (Target / Target[], and
    optional when the relation is nullable) — never 'any';
  * enum member keys are PascalCase;
  * no field option may be written at its default (canGroup/canSort/showInTable/
    editFromTable/canFilter are already true, readOnly/searchable already false);
  * @Enum/@MultiEnum take a global name ONLY when another entity shares the enum;
  * a relation target that already exists on the tenant gets a STUB — @Entity({name,key})
    + extends SystemBaseEntity, EMPTY body, its own file, registered in forFeature();
    a bare 'export class Accounts {}' registers nothing (E116), and stubs sharing a file
    are W616;
  * to ADD columns to an entity you do NOT own (a system entity, or another
    application's), declare an EXTENSION — the entity's existing name, only your own
    columns, in <owner>.extension.entity.ts. Extension mode ignores entity options
    (W618), refuses @OneToMany/@ManyToManyBackRef (E118) and primary: true (E119),
    requires a default with nullable: false (E120), and allows @Index/@Check over your
    own columns only, listed literally (E121/E122). Write every options object
    out literally: one passed by reference or spread hides all of that (E123). A
    relation there names its target by string and is typed by shape — that form
    is W620 anywhere else;
  * 'owner' comes first in a tabular part's importKeyFields, and no 'inverse' is passed
    to @ManyToOne/@ManyToMany.
Pass the app ROOT, not one file: several rules read the whole repo ("nothing references
this enum name" cannot be judged from a single file).
passed=false means fix and re-run — it is not advisory.

path.description: ABSOLUTE path to the application repo root (preferred), or to one *.entity.ts / *.seed.ts file.

strict.description: true (default): the house rules above (W607/W609-W613, W615-W623, W625, W626, W628, W634-W637, W640) fail the gate. false: they are reported as advisory — for a legacy repo you are not cleaning up in this pass, never for a file you just wrote. Errors, E116 included, block either way.

instructions:
Suppa Platform MCP Server — Tasks, Docs/Pages, Entities, Forms, Automations and file attachments on Suppa tenants.

AUTHENTICATION — RESOLVE THIS BEFORE ANY OTHER SUPPA WORK
- Sign-in is an interactive Google flow in the browser. There is NO API key for a user to find or paste — NEVER ask for a token, key or password; call suppa_login instead.
- Signed in? suppa_list_tenants shows the STORED "authenticated"/"needs_login" (no network; a revoked session still reads signed in); suppa_diagnostics makes the live call that settles it.
- When not signed in — or any tool answers "No credentials" / HTTP 401 / "session could not be refreshed" / ReloginRequired — DO NOT STOP and DO NOT ask for a key:
    1. Call suppa_login (suppa_login(tenant="<alias|host|url>") targets another instance; default is the active tenant). It OPENS A GOOGLE SIGN-IN PAGE in the default browser, served locally at http://localhost:8080.
    2. Tell the user: "I've opened a Google sign-in page in your browser — pick your account to finish signing in." If the browser did not open, the result carries the URL for them to open by hand.
    3. It blocks until they finish and returns {"status":"ok"} — THEN retry the original action. Tokens go to the OS keychain and auto-refresh: one login per tenant, not per session.
- A static SUPPA_API_KEY in the client env (CI / single tenant) means no login is needed; it is optional and most users have none.
- suppa_diagnostics validates the whole setup and reports the login_origin to whitelist. ONE-TIME ORG SETUP: http://localhost:8080 must be in the Google OAuth client's "Authorized JavaScript origins" — a sign-in page that opens but never completes is almost always this; tell the user so an admin can add it.
- suppa_use_tenant switches the active instance for ALL later calls; suppa_list_tenants shows what is known and authenticated.

DATA BASICS
- IDs are integers, not UUIDs. Dates are ISO-8601; a naive datetime (no offset) is read as UTC, so pass an explicit offset (+03:00) or convert local times yourself. Task deadlines also accept 'today', 'tomorrow', '+3d', '+2h', '+30m', '+1w'.
- Each write tool's description states the shapes it demands — relations and enums as {"id": N}, list fields REPLACED unless merge_json says otherwise — and validates against the live schema before writing. Read it before calling: a bare number where a reference belongs returns 201 and stores null.
- DELETE IS A SOFT DELETE — every delete tool sets deletedAt and leaves the row in place, reversible with suppa_restore_record(entity_name, record_id); never tell the user their data was destroyed. It still needs confirm=true because the row leaves all normal reads; find it again with deleted_scope='deleted'.
- PERMANENT DELETE IS UNAVAILABLE HERE, BY DESIGN — this server performs REVERSIBLE deletes only. The platform's PERMANENT delete (POST /core/data/:entityName/delete — rows leave the table and cannot be restored) is BLOCKED in the HTTP client itself: no tool, flag, confirm=true or direct call reaches it, and an attempt is refused before any request is sent. Do not look for a tool, a parameter or a workaround — there is none. Asked to erase data for good, say so plainly and offer the soft delete (suppa_delete_record → /remove, undone by suppa_restore_record); permanent removal is an admin action in the platform's own UI.
- Reads are compact: relation objects omit deletedAt when null (a live row); schema reads omit nulls, false flags and default options and carry a _legend (full=true returns the raw form).

SEARCH & FILTERS — suppa_search_records' description carries the comparators, nested AND/OR groups, dotted field paths, "$current-user", paging and the auto-diagnosis of an empty result. Read it before your first search.
- PROJECT ONLY THE FIELDS YOU NEED: fields_json is on suppa_search_records AND on every task/doc read (suppa_get_task, suppa_search_tasks — which also takes task_ids, so several tasks are ONE call, never one suppa_get_task each — suppa_get_doc, suppa_list_pages, …). WRITING ENTITY CODE (*.entity.ts in an application repo — NOT the API tools above)
These seven rules are house rules of this platform. They OVERRIDE the platform's own migrations doc (which contradicts two of them) and the style of the entities already in the repo you are editing — a file that breaks them is the habit these rules exist to stop, not a convention to match. Full skill: skills/suppa-entity-code/SKILL.md in the installed suppa-mcp-2 package; the seven bind whether or not you open it.
1. TYPE EVERY RELATION PROPERTY to match its decorator: @ManyToOne -> `owner: Target;` (`owner?: Target` when the relation is nullable); @ManyToMany/@OneToMany/@ManyToManyBackRef -> `peers: Target[];`. Never `any`.
2. ENUM MEMBER KEYS ARE PascalCase — `NotFilled = 'Not filled'` — the stored value is the string on the right and need not match the key.
3. NEVER WRITE A FIELD OPTION AT ITS DEFAULT: canGroup, canSort, showInTable, editFromTable and canFilter are already true; readOnly and searchable are already false. Write one ONLY where the field departs from that (usually just `searchable: true`); all seven spelled out is wrong even though it works.
4. @Enum/@MultiEnum TAKE THE GLOBAL NAME ONLY WHEN THE ENUM IS GLOBAL — one value set shared by several entities (a seed writes the bare value and needs none). Otherwise omit the first argument: `@Enum(StatusEnum, StatusTitles, { … })` derives <@Entity name>.<field name> — the entity's NAME, not its class. A field's own `key: 'Entity.field'` is the rename key, NOT a reference, and does not make the enum global. Key the titles map by VALUE: `[StatusEnum.Active]: { title }` (W637).
5. A RELATION TARGET THAT ALREADY EXISTS on the tenant (created earlier, or owned by another application) gets a STUB — three things at once: `@Entity({ name: 'Accounts', key: 'Accounts' }) export class Accounts extends SystemBaseEntity {}` with an EMPTY body, ALONE in a file named `accounts.stub.entity.ts`, and REGISTERED in forFeature() with the entities you create. Never a bare `export class Accounts {}` — it satisfies the thunk but registers nothing, so the platform cannot resolve the relation (E116). Never fields on a stub — it only lets a relation point at the table (E117); to ADD columns there, see rule 6. Platform system entities need no stub: import UsersEntity/FilesEntity/IconsEntity from @suppa/sdk.
6. TO ADD COLUMNS TO AN ENTITY YOU DO NOT OWN, DECLARE AN EXTENSION — not a stub; there is no separate API. Declare the entity by its EXISTING name with only your own columns, in `<owner-entity>.extension.entity.ts` (class `<OwnerEntity>Extension`), registered like any other entity: `@Entity({ name: 'Users' }) export class UsersExtension extends SystemBaseEntity { @Column({ type: FieldTypeEnum.Numeric, nullable: true }) accountId?: number; }`. The platform picks the mode by OWNERSHIP at start. In extension mode: entity options are IGNORED (title/icon/type/options/representativeFieldName/importKeyFields — W618); no @OneToMany or @ManyToManyBackRef (E118); no `primary: true` (E119); no `nullable: false` without a default (E120); @Index/@Check only over your own columns, listed as a literal array (E121/E122). Write @Entity()/@Column() options as literal objects — one passed by reference or through a spread cannot be read, so none of this can be checked on it (E123). A relation to an entity you do not own takes NO string target - name it on a raw column (W620): `@Column({ type: RelationTypeEnum.ManyToOne, relationEntityName: 'Invoices', relationFieldName: 'id' }) invoice?: { id: number };`.
7. CUSTOM FIELDS IN CODE need @suppa/sdk 1.38.0 (E129) and a nested class of columns that is NOT an entity — no @Entity(), never in forFeature() (E124: registering it breaks every custom-field read and write) — reached by a property that MUST be named customFields (E125): `@CustomFields(() => TasksCustomFields) customFields?: TasksCustomFields;`. Every column needs options.customFieldSets [{contextField (on the owner), contextValue (a value, not an id)}] or no record shows it (W621). SKILL.md rule 22; template custom-fields.template.ts.
